gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Govee's Star Light Projector (Ocean Wave, H6094) at $69.99 is a branded smart star-and-ocean projector that ships without a power adapter (Govee: 'use a standard 5V DC adapter', 5 V / 2 A / 10 W). Its radios use only the 2.4 GHz band (FCC 2A7VD-H6094). It works with the Govee Home app, Alexa, Google Assistant and Matter, but Govee's Matter FAQ says you need a Matter hub or controller, lists only on/off, brightness, colour temperature and colour as Matter features, and says Matter turns off if you switch networks in the Govee Home app.
standout_why: I tried to read every rival page and none would open. Walmart 20631755363 (cited) and the business.walmart.com copy showed a bot-check page. glarexx.com returned HTTP 429 twice. retrowave.online and sientle.com failed SSL checks. The cited YouTube review returned only the page footer, and bestproductsreviews.com returned an empty page. From what can be seen (the result titles and ChatGPT's answer), the results are unbranded 'smart 5D holographic' USB night lights. ChatGPT's own answer says their 'smart connectivity' is 'not independently verified'. None of the results names a maker with an app, voice assistant or Matter, or gives an adapter rating. Because I could not read the rival pages themselves, this is a 2, not a 3.
decides: The shopper asked for a 'smart' star and ocean projector, which needs a named product with stated app and voice-assistant support. Govee H6094 is one, unlike the unbranded 5D listings ChatGPT showed. The page should give its two limits. First, budget for a 5 V / 2 A adapter because none is in the box. Second, Matter (Apple Home, SmartThings) needs a hub and Govee lists only on/off, brightness and colour as Matter features, so expect to use the Govee Home app or Alexa/Google for the scenes.

findings.label: Radio bands in FCC grant
findings.source_title: FCC ID 2A7VD-H6094 Govee Star Light Projector
findings.note: Grant dated 2025-09-25, equipment class DTS. The 2412–2472 MHz range matches 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi channels 1–13 and 2402–2480 MHz matches Bluetooth LE. The grant does not name the protocols; that reading is mine.

findings.label: Matter needs a hub
findings.value: Yes: 'a Matter hub—or a Matter controller is required' (e.g. HomePod mini / HomePod 2nd gen / Apple TV 4K on iOS 16.2+, Nest Hub 2nd gen, Echo devices, SmartThings hubs)
findings.note: The FAQ also requires a phone on a 2.4 GHz network and an IPv6 network. Matter setup must be finished within 15 minutes of powering the device on.

findings.label: Features exposed over Matter
findings.value: On/off, brightness, colour temperature, colour ('More features TBD')
findings.note: This is a general Govee FAQ. Its model list still names only the M1 strip and does not list H6094. Scenes and white-noise modes are not listed as Matter features.

findings.label: Matter exclusion
findings.value: Switching networks in the Govee Home app disables Matter
findings.note: FAQ wording: 'If you use the Govee Home App to switch networks during use, the Matter function of the device will be disabled.' It also says older Govee products are not supported because of their chips.
